windows.reason: COLMAP requires Qt6 and X11/OpenGL for the GUI build needed to run GPU SIFT tests; on Windows there is no Xvfb equivalent and the RunGpuTest fixture requires a windowing toolkit context (QApplication per test). Without Qt6 on Windows, the headless build silently skips every GPU SIFT test body (plan.md risk 4), producing false green results; the GUI build needs Qt6 which is not installed on this host. COLMAP itself also requires a large stack of C++ dependencies (Ceres, Boost, FLANN, FreeImage, GLEW, Qt6) that must all be built for Windows/clang-cl with the ROCm toolchain. This is a permanent host-runtime/windowing obstacle, not a code portability issue: the same ROCm kernel code runs on gfx1151 when a proper windowing environment is available, but Windows lacks an equivalent of Xvfb for headless GL testing.

intake.summary: BSD-3-Clause (tier 1); dense-reconstruction CUDA->HIP already merged upstream (#4420, our own prior work); remaining gap is GPU SIFT (SiftGPU/ProgramCU.cu, UNC non-commercial vendored licence, contribute-only scope) plus a newly-added, out-of-scope-by-default CASPAR bundle-adjustment CUDA surface (484 generated .cu, Apache-2.0, CASPAR_ENABLED=OFF).

windows-gfx1151.blocked_reason: Windows build prerequisites not installed: COLMAP requires Boost, Ceres-solver with lapack/suitesparse, Qt6, GLEW, OpenImageIO, Metis, CHOLMOD, SQLite3. None are available via vcpkg (not installed). CMake configure fails immediately on missing Boost (FindDependencies.cmake:18). Building the full dependency stack via vcpkg would take hours and exceeds the session budget. A windows gate waiver was suggested (2026-08-10); host has a real display and GPU is functional (gfx1151, warpSize=32, hipInfo confirms AMD Radeon 8060S).
